title: How Steve Jobs framed Apple's comeback, passion and talent: D5 joint interview with Bill Gates (2007)
summary: Onstage with Bill Gates at D5, Jobs explains why Apple stopped treating Microsoft as a zero-sum rival, why it sees itself as a software company, and why it partners instead of doing everything. He closes with advice on passion, scouting talent, and looking forward instead of back.

principles.text: Don't define yourself by beating a rival; remember who you are.
principles.quote: Apple didn't have to beat Microsoft. Apple had to remember who Apple was, because it'd forgotten who Apple was.

principles.text: Let go of past mistakes and build tomorrow.
principles.quote: And so, let's go invent tomorrow, rather than worrying about what happened yesterday.

principles.text: Passion is what lets you persevere through the hard parts.
principles.quote: And if you don't love it, you're going to fail. So you got to love it. You got to have passion, and I think that's the high order bit.

principles.text: Be a talent scout: great teams matter more than personal smarts.
principles.quote: Because no matter how smart you are, you need a team of great people, and you've got to figure out how to size people up fairly quickly

principles.text: Focus on what you're great at and partner for the rest.
principles.quote: We don't think one company can do everything. So you've got to partner with people that are really good at stuff.

principles.text: Great products come from editing: deciding what goes in and what stays out.
principles.quote: I think the art of it is balancing what's on there, and what's not on there. It's the editing function.
